scope: Independent Home/Store/Quest reference-comparison and non-destructive mobile composition diagnostics

referenceEvidence.normalization: Stored reference artifact; 1408x1056 comparison images are uniform-scale normalizations of the exact originals.

runningCaptureEvidence.note: This artifact is an exact historical render at its recorded head and is used for visual diagnosis only. It is not relabeled as a current-head or physical-device PASS.

rawPixelDiffDiagnosticOnly.method: Mean absolute RGB difference between same-size 1408x1056 normalized reference and exact running capture; no acceptance threshold is assigned.

findings: The reference is a warm, richly layered bedroom with strong material depth, luminous window light, dense side-zone props and a large expressive avatar occupying the visual center. The running capture is materially flatter, more abstract and more sparsely staged even though its real controls and state remain visible.
The current navy header and large progress chrome claim substantially more visual weight than the reference's top status strip, reducing the bedroom/character share of the viewport.

The lane-13 Home v2 material/palette/light improvements remain directionally correct, but reviewer-14's existing lower hero-corridor/phone-crop REWORK still controls; do not integrate v2 until that conflict is repaired.
Home.repairPriority: Keep the richer warm material/light language while clearing the lower-center avatar corridor and producing a deliberate phone crop/derivative; do not flatten UI or fake state to chase the reference.

findings: The reference makes the boutique and avatar try-on zone a major visual attraction: dimensional shelves/lighting, a large character, a luminous pink-heart accent and merchandise cards share the screen. The running capture is much more UI-dominant and architecturally flat, with the avatar confined to a comparatively small right-side stage.

The reference keeps the selected product action area visually tied to the large avatar and boutique scene. In the running capture the catalog grid, dream-goal band and heavy blue chrome compete strongly with try-on and selected-item presence.
Lane-13's separate boutique/background, avatar-stage and heart-wall-light component strategy is compositionally appropriate because it can restore depth without baking controls or prices into art.
Store.repairPriority: Increase boutique/try-on visual depth and avatar prominence while preserving the real catalog grid, selection state and purchase controls as separate live UI.

findings: The reference is a warm, storybook-like learning room with dense shelf/material detail, expressive character art and a visually rich story/question panel. The running capture preserves a clear real question/answer workflow but is substantially darker, flatter and more spatially empty around the learning panel.
The current white mission panel is readable, but the surrounding environment and character presentation do not approach the reference's warmth, depth or authored classroom/story context.
Any scene upgrade must remain behind the existing real prompt, answer options, hint and mastery state; no generated scene may encode an answer or substitute for learning content.
Quest.repairPriority: Use separate dimensional environment/character components to restore warm room depth and visual storytelling while keeping the real learning panel and answer semantics untouched.

Home: At 390x844 the room-progress panel consumes most of the initial upper viewport and the avatar/buddy are only partly established before the lower navigation; at 320x568 the hero is pushed even farther below the dominant progress card.

The progress controls remain legible, but the reference's character-first emotional hierarchy is weak on phone. Repair by compacting/composing the progress area and using an art-directed environment/hero crop rather than hiding live controls.
Store: At 390x844 the dream-goal and category controls precede the try-on stage; at 320x568 the initial viewport is almost entirely header, dream-goal and category chrome, so avatar/selected-item spectacle falls below the fold.

Category buttons remain large/readable, but the 320px view exposes only part of the horizontal category sequence at once. Preserve genuine scrolling/controls while giving the selected item/try-on composition an earlier visual foothold.
Quest: At both phone widths the character intro and large skill-mission card consume the initial viewport, while answer choices are below the fold. The prompt is readable, but the question-to-action loop is visually separated.
Reduce nonessential scene/hero vertical consumption on phone and keep prompt/answers spatially closer without altering wording, answer ordering, hint behavior or mastery logic.

handoff.15: Use these exact artifact-bound comparisons to prioritize Store selected-item/try-on depth, Quest warm material/context depth, and Home hero-corridor repair. Raw pixel diff remains diagnostic-only.
handoff.13: Continue separate environment/character/prop components, not flattened UI. Home v2 remains blocked by the existing lower-center hero corridor/phone crop issue; Store and Quest can continue with separable depth layers against these findings.
handoff.10: Mobile findings are visual composition diagnostics from headless Chromium only; do not convert them into physical-device or accessibility PASS claims.
